tools.name: search_places
tools.description: Search the named places OrbitStudio can open directly: craters, mountains, valleys, basins and spacecraft landing sites on the Moon and other worlds. Use it when the user names or describes a place to 3D print, or asks what there is on a world. Returns each match's world, coordinates, the size of it

tools.name: suggest_model
tools.description: Suggest OrbitStudio settings for a 3D-printed puzzle or ornament of a place, from the app's own defaults and the limits of that world's elevation data, plus a link that opens the app at the place with those settings filled in, ready for the user to press Generate. Use it when the user wants to make

tools.name: get_preview
tools.description: Return pictures already published on orbitstudio3d.com for a world or a place: photos of printed models, renders made with the app, and the world's map texture, each captioned with what it shows. Use it when the user wants to see what a model looks like. Nothing is rendered on request.

tools.name: list_worlds
tools.description: List the worlds OrbitStudio currently offers, with each world's size, number of known places, default relief, smallest selection and data caveats. Use it when the user asks which planets or moons can be printed.

tools.name: get_product_info
tools.description: Facts about OrbitStudio: what it makes, its two tools and the worlds offered, which steps are free and which are not, a link to the page that lists the plans, and the support address. Use it when the user asks what OrbitStudio is or which parts of it are free.

tools.name: star_map_link
tools.description: Build a link that opens OrbitStudio Sky with the night sky over a place on Earth at a local date and time, as a 3D-printable star map plate. Use it for a birth, wedding or 'night we met' star map. Give a place name, which is looked up on OpenStreetMap, or latitude and longitude, which win when both
